categories.main_business_segments: Fuji Die Co., Ltd. and its group companies operate a single business segment focused on the manufacturing and sales of wear-resistant tools and cemented carbide materials. Their primary products include cemented carbide tools, dies, and related components, serving a wide range of industrial applications. The group also manufactures and sells steel, ceramics, and other non-carbide wear-resistant products. The business is conducted through the parent company and seven subsidiaries (two domestic, five overseas).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core technologies are based on powder metallurgy, particularly the production of cemented carbide materials by mixing metal carbides (mainly tungsten carbide) with cobalt and other binders, forming and sintering at high temperatures. They possess advanced precision machining and inspection technologies, enabling high-precision, high-durability custom tools and dies. The group maintains an integrated production system covering powder mixing, sintering, machining, and inspection, and is actively developing new materials and ultra-precision processing methods, including for next-generation applications.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Fuji Die serves a diverse industrial customer base, including the automotive, steel, non-ferrous metals, beverage can manufacturing, electrical/electronics, and machinery sectors. Their products are used in the production of automotive parts, metal products, batteries, semiconductors, and various industrial components. The company primarily supplies B2B customers, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of sales.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Japan and Asia, with sales offices and production sites in Japan, China, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and India (currently dormant). Sales are also made to North America and other regions. In FY2025, approximately 80% of sales were in Japan, with the remainder in Asia and other regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Fuji Die operates midstream in the supply chain, producing intermediate and finished wear-resistant tools and dies used in customers' manufacturing processes. They source raw materials (mainly tungsten carbide and cobalt) from upstream suppliers, process them into tools and dies, and supply these to downstream manufacturers in various industries.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening the management foundation, improving productivity and efficiency (notably through automation and digitalization), expanding overseas business, contributing to decarbonization and a circular economy, and establishing new businesses. R&D focuses on new materials (including low-tungsten/cobalt alloys and recycling), ultra-precision processing, and products for next-generation automotive, energy, and optical communications markets. The company is also developing electrodes for green hydrogen production and expanding its recycling initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of custom-made and standard wear-resistant tools, dies, and related materials. Revenue is recognized at the point of delivery to customers, with most transactions being one-off sales based on customer orders. There are no significant recurring revenue streams such as subscriptions or licensing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Fuji Die is positioned as a specialized manufacturer of cemented carbide wear-resistant tools and dies, competing with other Japanese and global toolmakers such as Sumitomo Electric, Mitsubishi Materials, and Hitachi Tool Engineering. The company differentiates itself through custom solutions, integrated production, and advanced powder metallurgy and precision processing technologies. It is a mid-sized player with a strong reputation in niche, high-precision applications.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, consolidated net sales were 16.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 488 million yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 426 million yen. The company has around 1,090 consolidated employees. Growth has been relatively flat in recent years, with a slight sales decline in FY2025 and profitability impacted by raw material costs and investments in IT and personnel. Overseas sales are targeted for expansion, aiming for 25% of total sales by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Fuji Die emphasizes high precision, long life, and customization in its wear-resistant tools and dies, leveraging advanced powder metallurgy and ultra-precision machining. The integrated production system allows for flexible, small-lot, multi-variety manufacturing tailored to customer needs. The company also highlights its commitment to sustainability through recycling, resource-saving materials, and products supporting next-generation industries such as EVs and green energy.
